diff.content:
diff --git a/watcher/gate.py b/watcher/gate.py
--- a/watcher/gate.py
+++ b/watcher/gate.py
@@ -1058,13 +1058,9 @@ def build_is_mergeable(status, run_failures, job_failures, unread_comments):
     if not status["fully_settled"]:
         return False
-    if status["red_count"] > 0 or status["waiting_count"] > 0:
+    if status["waiting_count"] > 0:
         return False
-    if int(status.get("aborted_count") or 0) > 0:
+    if has_gating_failure(status, run_failures, job_failures):
         return False
-    # A settled status view can still hide an aborted or red run underneath;
-    # accept the candidate only once neither signal objects.
-    if run_failures or job_failures:
-        return False
     if unread_comments:
         return False
     return True
diff --git a/tests/test_gate.py b/tests/test_gate.py
--- a/tests/test_gate.py
+++ b/tests/test_gate.py
@@ -20,1 +20,10 @@ def test_build_is_mergeable_rejects_a_waiting_run():
     assert not build_is_mergeable(waiting_status(), [], [], [])
+
+
+def test_build_is_mergeable_uses_the_shared_gating_predicate():
+    status = settled_status(aborted_count=1)
+    assert not build_is_mergeable(status, [], [], [])
+
+
+def test_build_is_mergeable_still_rejects_a_job_failure(monkeypatch):
+    assert not build_is_mergeable(settled_status(), [], ["job-1"], [])

change_contract.goal: Route the last inline copy of the gating-failure policy through the shared `has_gating_failure` predicate that two other agreement sites already use.
acceptance_criteria: `build_is_mergeable` uses the shared predicate instead of its own inline conditions for aborted and red runs.
non_goals: Change what `has_gating_failure` itself considers a failure.
preserved_behaviors: A waiting run still rejects the candidate.
A settled, fully green candidate with no unread comments is still accepted.

repository_instructions.label: Shared-policy rules
repository_instructions.summary: A policy predicate with more than one call site must have exactly one implementation. An inline copy at a remaining call site is a defect once the shared version exists, not a stylistic choice.

nearby_patterns.label: Two call sites already using the shared predicate

data: `has_gating_failure(status, run_failures, job_failures)` already exists in `watcher/policy.py` and is already called from two other agreement sites in `watcher/reconcile.py`.
This inline copy in `build_is_mergeable` predates the shared predicate and was never migrated when the predicate was introduced.
The same duplication class previously caused two separate incidents where one call site's copy drifted from another's and produced a self-contradictory result for the same candidate.
operational: `build_is_mergeable` is the gate a merge automation checks before acting, so a wrong answer here is user-visible.
